root_idea.summary: The root centers on striking or colliding with the horns, with extensions to facing one another, conflict, ominous encounters, and resulting hardship.
root_idea.development: The physical act of horn-striking develops into reciprocal collision and figurative contention; what confronts one from the front can become an omen, and severe events are described as blows or clashes.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized feminine lexical noun نَطِيحَة rather than the inflected QAC surface form.

senses.definition: An animal gored by another animal's horns and thereby killed.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic dietary context, نَطِيحَة is a substantivized designation for livestock killed by goring; it is listed among animals whose flesh is prohibited because of the manner of death.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To strike another with the horn.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The basic transitive use, especially of a ram or other horned animal striking another creature.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To push or thrust someone away and remove him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of striking or driving someone off.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For two animals to strike one another with their horns.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal construction used of rams, he-goats, and similar horned animals.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Contention or dispute likened to the clashing of two rams.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use applied, among others, to contention between learned men or between merchants.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To face, confront, or stand opposite another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A dialectal use, especially reported for the Hijaz, in which نِطَاحٌ can denote مقابلة, facing or confrontation.
Used of waves and torrents, and by extension of combatants clashing in battle.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An animal or bird that comes toward one from in front and is treated as an omen.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may refer to birds or wild animals encountered from before one, whose course is used to augur good or evil.
A figurative extension from the ominous creature or encounter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A horse with a distinctive facial marking regarded as unlucky.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is applied to a horse whose blaze reaches one ear or whose forehead has two disliked circular or spiral hair-curls.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A ram that strikes repeatedly with its horn; figuratively, a person who pushes or thrusts persistently or vehemently.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The intensive form describes repeated or forceful horn-striking and its figurative application to a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A difficulty, affliction, calamity, or other distressing event.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in expressions for a hardship that befalls someone, including the hardships of fortune.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The two stars of Aries associated with the horns of the Ram, also treated as a lunar mansion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The astronomical name may occur with or without the definite article; its rising was traditionally associated with prognostication.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the expression مَا لَهُ نَاطِحٌ وَلَا خَابِطٌ, a sheep or goat, contrasted with a camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a specialized idiomatic noun use within the cited expression.
